newsitem.title: USA: New York City to sublet Brooklyn hospital to PHS.
newsitem.headline: New York City to sublet Brooklyn hospital to PHS.

text.p: New York City, which is trying to sell three of its hospitals, said on Thursday it reached an agreement to sublet Cooney Island Hospital to a for-profit company, PHS NY Inc.
The agreement calls for PHS NY to sublet the hospital, which is located in Brooklyn, for 99 years. When the deal closes, PHS NY will pay $42.1 million to the city's Health and Hospitals Corp.
The company, an affiliate of PHS Inc, which runs health-care companies in Cleveland and Philadelphia, also will pay $6.9 million to amortize debt linked to the hospital after the initial payment.
A key issue raised by some community groups has been whether service to indigent patients will be protected after hopsitals are privatized.
The agreement with PHS NY would require it to maintain the current level of service and to be prepared to spend an additional amount indexed to inflation.

In mid-August, the city comptroller raised a number of concerns about a preliminary agreement that was reached with PHS NY, including questioning whether it would in fact save the city the $100 million as estimated.
